gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the picks' tyre-inflation claims on the same tyre and pressure range. GOOLOO rates the A3 at 0→36 PSI on a small 205/55 R16 car tyre in under 7 min. WOLFBOX rates its 45 L/min MegaVolt 24Air at a 30→36 PSI top-up on a 275/70 R17 SUV tyre in 1 min 20 s. TechGearLab timed the MegaVolt16 Air, ChatGPT's 'best tested' pick, at 3 min to add 5 PSI to a 275/70 R18 F-150 tyre (about 1.7 PSI/min, against the 4.5 PSI/min WOLFBOX claims for the 24Air on a near-identical tyre).
standout_why: I compared against TechGearLab's MegaVolt16 Air review (cited), TechGearLab's best-jump-starter list, gearmyride.com and autoboosting.com. I couldn't open Popular Mechanics, the cited GOOLOO page; it returned a fetch error. TechGearLab gives only the one '5 PSI in 3 minutes' figure, and its list gives no numeric inflation results. Gearmyride lists max PSI and L/min and says 'maximum PSI is not the same as inflation speed', but it never sets the makers' inflation claims side by side. Autoboosting notes that airflow units vary (SLPM vs L/min) and that peak amps 'aren't measured the same way across brands', but it doesn't convert anything. None of these pages lines up the makers' inflation claims, each on a different tyre and PSI range, or compares WOLFBOX's claim with TechGearLab's measured time. None converts GOOLOO's mAh rating to Wh either.
decides: This mostly confirms the pick and corrects how it's framed. Max PSI (150 vs 160) tells the shopper nothing, because every quoted inflation time uses a different tyre and pressure range. For topping up a sedan or crossover tyre, the cheaper GOOLOO A3 is not shown to be slower than the WOLFBOX. Two things also matter for the pick. First, the A3 costs $69.99 on gooloo.com today; ChatGPT's $89.99 is the price of the A3 Pro. Second, the MegaVolt16 Air costs $179.40 at wolfbox.com, not 'around $110'. The only independent measurement, TechGearLab's, has the MegaVolt16 Air taking 3 minutes per 5 PSI on a full-size truck tyre. That is below what WOLFBOX claims for the 45 L/min 24Air on a similar tyre, so a pickup owner who picks the 4000A 24Air for the bigger tyre is buying peak amps, not faster inflation that anyone has measured.
